pcf-secret-replication.overview: Studies pseudorandom correlation functions built from symmetric cryptography and secret replication to shrink the material exchanged during preprocessing.
pcf-secret-replication.reading: A PLLM candidate must name the correlation distribution, sharing domain, fresh-use rule, and expansion costs before it can replace any existing preparation source.

finite-field-pcg.overview: Constructs pseudorandom correlated material over general finite fields instead of assuming one fixed arithmetic domain.
finite-field-pcg.reading: Field-specific material cannot silently substitute for the integer-ring corrections in PLLM's prepared runtime; bind its consumer and modulus first.

sparse-unit-correlations.overview: Uses sparse pseudorandom generators to compress unit-vector correlations used in secure computation.
sparse-unit-correlations.reading: Measure seed expansion, density, recipient shares, and downstream consumption together; smaller seeds alone do not establish cheaper inference.

mozzarella.overview: Presents vector-Oblivious Linear Evaluation and zero-knowledge techniques over powers-of-two rings.
mozzarella.reading: The publisher PDF is not in PLLM's verified library. An implementation needs the original protocol and ring/security checks, not a citation-based substitute.

ring-lpn-pcg.overview: Derives pseudorandom correlations from ring-LPN assumptions as an alternative to directly communicating all preprocessing material.
ring-lpn-pcg.reading: A candidate must specify the assumption, attack parameters, ring, consumers, and expansion cost; this is not a general-purpose mask seed.

silent-ot.overview: Extends oblivious transfer with compact correlated seeds that can be expanded into a larger supply of transfer material.
silent-ot.reading: Count setup, local expansion, memory, failure handling, and the online protocol that consumes each transfer before comparing with PLLM preparation.

compressing-vole.overview: Compresses vector oblivious linear-evaluation correlations for later use in secure arithmetic protocols.
compressing-vole.reading: Treat the arithmetic field, share holders, distribution, and one-use policy as part of the component contract, not an interchangeable byte format.

bifrost.overview: Combines trusted execution and homomorphic encryption for transformer and LLM serving, placing work across different trust mechanisms.
bifrost.reading: Its TEE and encryption boundary is a different deployment choice from PLLM's non-colluding prepared roles; compare full roles and costs before claiming equivalence.

shaft.overview: Targets transformer inference with secure computation while jointly considering accuracy and execution cost.
shaft.reading: Separate its numerical choices from protocol and deployment choices, then test quality, traffic, and latency under a matched transformer workload.

llama-math.overview: Develops lower-latency secure arithmetic for nonlinear mathematical operations used in neural inference; LLAMA here is a math library, not Meta's model family.
llama-math.reading: Adapt one bounded operation with exact rounding and sharing contracts before interpreting a scalar improvement as a decoder speedup.

sirnn.overview: Provides secure mathematical building blocks for recurrent-network inference, where fixed-point nonlinear functions need protected evaluation.
sirnn.reading: PLLM must validate its own operator domain and model-quality effects; an RNN library does not supply a complete private LLM decoder.

atlas.overview: Automates approximation choices for encrypted transformer operations to reduce homomorphic-evaluation cost.
atlas.reading: Represent approximation error, workload, and ciphertext costs as typed constraints; no ATLAS search result is a measured PLLM inference result.

encformer.overview: Designs transformer inference over encrypted data with attention to the cost of evaluating model operators securely.
encformer.reading: A ciphertext-oriented execution path needs its own numeric and key lifecycle, not a drop-in replacement for prepared masked-linear stages.

rosetta.overview: Combines CKKS and TFHE to evaluate parts of private language-model decoding across two homomorphic-encryption styles.
rosetta.reading: Before comparison, model conversions, keys, precision, recurrent token feedback, and the complete decoding workload must be included.

breaking-layer-barrier.overview: Reorganizes protected transformer execution across CKKS and MPC so that expensive layer-by-layer interactions can be reconsidered.
breaking-layer-barrier.reading: A PLLM compiler candidate needs explicit conversion and residency contracts; changing a schedule alone does not remove online communication.

cipherprune.overview: Prunes transformer work to reduce encrypted or private inference cost, making model behavior part of the optimization decision.
cipherprune.reading: Keep quality and compatibility gates beside protocol metrics; fewer operations cannot be ranked without a matched checkpoint and output task.

ditto.overview: Studies quantization choices for MPC transformer inference, where arithmetic width and approximation affect both correctness and private-computation cost.
ditto.reading: PLLM would bind quantization to a plan and compare private bytes, latency, and model quality, not reuse clear-model quantization evidence.

mpc-minimized.overview: Reduces the portion of LLM inference that requires MPC by choosing which operations need protected interaction.
mpc-minimized.reading: The moved operations must still meet PLLM's prompt and activation privacy contract; include remaining client work in any comparison.

mpcformer.overview: Reworks transformer operations for private MPC execution, trading numerical approximation and interaction cost.
mpcformer.reading: Evaluate one bounded operator before full-decoder claims, then measure end-to-end quality and all online rounds.

mosaic.overview: Uses masked outsourcing to allocate secure AI computation across parties with distinct access to model and inputs.
mosaic.reading: Its role and mask-release assumptions must be specified independently before it can be compared with PLLM's prepared public-weight path.

maverick.overview: Studies private, verifiable LLM inference through delegated matrix-vector multiplication and associated checks.
maverick.reading: This is a candidate protocol, not a measured PLLM reproduction; identify its parties, verification soundness, and entire decode cost first.

emvp.overview: Delegates encrypted matrix-vector products using secret dual codes, aiming to make linear work cheaper under its encoding assumptions.
emvp.reading: A prototype needs exact matrix orientation, code-parameter security, client cost, and output fidelity on a bounded stage.

sort-sweep-mirror.overview: Batches private interval lookups by organizing range comparisons so repeated queries share work rather than each building an independent scan.
sort-sweep-mirror.reading: A PLLM lookup candidate needs the same interval domain, private selection and leakage contract; measure the full batch, setup, and decoder handoff.

moai.overview: Proposes an architecture for non-interactive secure transformer inference that reorganizes model modules to fit its protocol.
moai.reading: The OpenReview PDF is inaccessible to PLLM's source acquisition; do not infer implementation details or runnable support from the title.

shark.overview: Targets actively secure inference with function secret sharing, adding malicious-adversary requirements to protected evaluation.
shark.reading: Active-security material, online role count, and abort semantics cannot be inherited from PLLM's honest-but-curious baseline.

thor.overview: Studies homomorphic-encryption-based transformer inference and the associated protected operator costs.
thor.reading: Treat keys, ciphertext depth, precision, and generation feedback as a separate deployment contract before ranking against prepared inference.

bolt.overview: Optimizes secure transformer inference while measuring both accuracy and execution efficiency.
bolt.reading: A PLLM comparison must preserve the same numeric and task-quality envelope as well as party topology and full response latency.

fastquery.overview: Reduces the communication cost of private embedding-table queries for language-model inference.
fastquery.reading: PLLM's public model path already performs token lookup locally; a protected lookup candidate needs a different deployment requirement and comparable privacy target.

nimbus.overview: Builds a two-party transformer inference system, choosing secure operators with attention to overall computation and communication.
nimbus.reading: Two online share holders are a different trust topology from PLLM's one online inference provider; keep both roles in the benchmark.

orca.overview: Explores GPU kernels for function-secret-sharing-based secure training and inference.
orca.reading: Accelerating a kernel does not eliminate per-party communication or preparation; assess a complete supported operator sequence.

ciphergpt.overview: Designs a secure two-party GPT inference protocol with protected transformer and generation operations.
ciphergpt.reading: An evaluation must account for both parties, exact token loop, cache state, and model quality before comparing with PLLM serving.

flute.overview: Speeds private lookup-table evaluation, a useful primitive when nonlinear functions are represented as tables.
flute.reading: Measure the full table, key material, private selection, conversion, and repetition costs for one decoder operator.

grotto.overview: Uses distributed point functions in a two-plus-one-party arrangement for protected arithmetic over powers-of-two rings.
grotto.reading: The helper and fresh-key supply are part of the protocol; it cannot be presented as a one-party lookup optimization.

puma.overview: Reports secure inference for a LLaMA-sized model, making full-model communication and runtime central to its result.
puma.reading: Compare its protected workload, hardware, parties, and token-generation semantics rather than reusing its headline latency in a different cohort.

primer.overview: Investigates faster transformer inference over encrypted data with operator-specific encrypted-evaluation choices.
primer.reading: Capture encryption keys, numeric precision, conversion work, and supported decoder state before treating it as a serving alternative.

cheetah.overview: Accelerates secure two-party neural-network inference with communication- and computation-aware protocols.
cheetah.reading: Its DNN techniques are reference inputs, not automatically whole-transformer operators; compare the exact topology and model task.

iron.overview: Studies private transformer inference, including the protected operators and exchanges needed by the architecture.
iron.reading: A paper-reported transformer result needs matching architecture, sequence length, two-party trust, and quality to serve as a PLLM baseline.

pika.overview: Extends function-secret-sharing secure computation to integer rings as a building block for protected operators.
pika.reading: Bind its ring, shares, keys, role holders, and error behavior before offering any decoder operator as a PLLM component.

the-x.overview: Uses homomorphic encryption for privacy-preserving transformer inference.
the-x.reading: Checkpoint, precision, ciphertext cost, and online autoregressive behavior must match before comparing with PLLM's public-weight baseline.

aby2.overview: Improves mixed-protocol two-party secure computation, where Boolean and arithmetic work can use different representations.
aby2.reading: Represent every cross-domain conversion and both online roles explicitly when using it as an operator-level reference.

fss-mixed.overview: Develops function secret sharing for fixed-point and mixed-mode secure operations.
fss-mixed.reading: Integer scales, truncation, FSS keys, and party placement are first-class requirements, not merely implementation parameters.

cryptflow2.overview: Implements practical two-party inference with explicit secure arithmetic and interaction tradeoffs.
cryptflow2.reading: A PLLM comparison requires identical numerical and privacy goals and must include its complete interactive schedule.

mixed-arithmetic-primitives.overview: Supplies MPC primitives for computation that switches between arithmetic and binary representations.
mixed-arithmetic-primitives.reading: Quantify each conversion and its security assumption before placing one primitive into a protected decoder plan.

silent-nisc.overview: Combines efficient oblivious-transfer extension with preprocessing for non-interactive secure computation.
silent-nisc.reading: Determine what counts as offline setup, which parties remain online, and how often its material must be renewed.

garbled-nn.overview: Studies the feasibility of garbled neural-network evaluation and the costs of carrying protected values through layers.
garbled-nn.reading: PLLM's isolated garbled kernels have not been composed into a comparable private model; account for the entire circuit and key supply.

fss-preprocessing.overview: Uses function secret sharing with preprocessing to enable later secure computations from prepared keys.
fss-preprocessing.reading: Bind key generation, distribution, one-use consumption, and the online sharing topology before comparing setup or latency.

gazelle.overview: Combines homomorphic linear work with garbled nonlinear work for low-latency secure neural-network inference.
gazelle.reading: Count conversion and preprocessing between these protected representations; a DNN stage is not a measured PLLM decoder.

cryptonets.overview: Demonstrates encrypted neural-network inference with homomorphic computation on model-friendly operators.
cryptonets.reading: Its feed-forward encrypted workload cannot establish private autoregressive generation or matched latency on PLLM's checkpoint.

fss-extensions.overview: Extends function secret sharing to a wider family of distributed functions and efficiency choices.
fss-extensions.reading: Evaluate one bounded function, key size, and party arrangement; title-level discovery is not evidence of protocol compatibility.

fss-original.overview: Introduces function secret sharing, distributing compact function keys among parties that evaluate shares of a function.
fss-original.reading: The original key-sharing contract belongs in a two- or multi-party protocol, not the single inference role of PLLM's prepared baseline.

breaking-euston.overview: Analyzes subspace leakage in secure inference and shows how private inputs can be recovered under a vulnerable masking construction.
breaking-euston.reading: Treat its attack as a required adversarial control for any proposed replacement mask; current masking semantics are not automatically vulnerable.

euston.overview: Pursues non-interactive secure transformer inference with a masking and outsourcing design.
euston.reading: An adaptation must pass subspace-leakage tests before it can be considered for either preparation or online masked work.

sok-transformers.overview: Surveys private transformer inference across systems, model designs, and cryptographic approaches rather than proposing one runtime component.
sok-transformers.reading: Use it to design fair workloads and threat-model comparisons; it does not authorize a new executable PLLM method.

game-of-arrows.overview: Studies attacks on weight obfuscation for on-device, TEE-shielded LLM partitioning.
game-of-arrows.reading: Apply it as an attack-aware review lens when hiding weights or partitioning trust, not as a faster inference protocol.

ripple.overview: A wavelet-based homomorphic lookup proposal appears as a research lead in Curl's references; PLLM has not verified an independent primary publication.
ripple.reading: Do not cite Curl's PDF as Ripple's original paper or create an executable lookup component until a standalone source is identified.

private-gpt-no-autoregression.overview: Examines private GPT workloads that avoid token-by-token autoregressive decoding.
private-gpt-no-autoregression.reading: Its generation objective differs from interactive decode; separate workload-level quality and functionality before comparing latency.

cachemir.overview: Studies fully homomorphic generative LLM inference with attention to persistent KV-cache state.
cachemir.reading: A cache candidate must preserve private state and exact token feedback; encrypted-cache performance requires a distinct full-model cohort.

deepprove.overview: Targets verifiable end-to-end LLM inference rather than checking only one linear stage.
deepprove.reading: Identify the precise proof statement, trusted setup, verifier work, and covered decode state before claiming whole-response integrity.

lamp.overview: Uses proximity testing to verify linear matrix multiplication claims.
lamp.reading: Compare detection probability, verifier cost, field bounds, and session attempt budgets with the existing bounded Freivalds check.

laminate.overview: Investigates succinct verifiability for SIMD-friendly fully homomorphic evaluation.
laminate.reading: Proof generation and verification attach to a different encrypted-execution contract; they do not automatically verify PLLM's prepared stages.

matrix-coding-verification.overview: Uses coding theory to verify an asserted full matrix product, including cases where the product error is sparse.
matrix-coding-verification.reading: Its AB = C claim is not PLLM's delegated W·x stage claim. First identify a compatible bounded subproblem before comparing challenge or verifier costs.
